To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the level of material toughened in alumina, as measured from the near-tip moire fringe data, is 2.5-5 times larger than that measured from the bulk mode I compliance, (2) the near-tip moiré data are consistent with a crack bridging toughening mechanism, and (3) the level of toughening increases with increasing grain size.
(a) grain boundary friction is an important toughening mechanism in alumina and (b) grain boundary friction toughening is enhanced by increasing grain size.

the R curves for nominally pure aluminate are dominated by the crack bridging process, that the bridging process is characterized by a single length scale, and that the length scale of crack bridging is determined by the grain size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding toughening in nominally pure, medium to large grain sized alumina.
the toughening of alumina and the effect of grain size.
the development of a quantitative model for the R-curve behavior of polycrystalline alumina.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the toughening mechanisms of crack bridging, friction, and grain boundary sliding are operative in nominally pure polycrystalline alumina.
grain size does not significantly affect the toughening level of nominally pure alumia.

the toughening due to grain boundary sliding is not a significant toughening mechanism in the alumina materials studied, and that the toughening that is observed in the R curve is due to the bridging of the crack by the alumina grains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for the alumina studied here the R curves are dominated by the singular crack tip stress fields, and that nonsingular toughening processes are not as significant as previously thought.
the toughening arising from the nonsingular bridging process is a function of the grain size and the grain boundary friction is a function of both the grain size and grain boundary character.
the toughening due to the nonsingular mechanisms is independent of the grain size and that the toughening is due to the bridging mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there exists a critical grain size below which the R-curve behavior is insensitive to grain size.
the grain size dependence of R-curve behavior can be explained by the relative contributions of the nonsingular toughening processes of crack bridgng and grain boundary friction.
, for a given alumina grain size, the near tip moiré R curves are higher than their bulk mode I counterparts, indicating that the material toughening is dominated by the nonsingular processes.
